title: Minimax Proximal ATE Estimation under Fixed Overlap with Low-Smoothness Nuisances
banked_reason: D0.5 achieved subfield below the field floor (paper-score ceiling 6.7 < 7.4); the rough unequal-smoothness converse remains open, and the upper variance proof and interval calibration have unresolved gaps.
gap_reasons: The proposed matched rough unequal-smoothness minimax frontier is not delivered: this theorem gives only a max-smoothness lower bound versus a sum-smoothness upper bound, with the needed direct-mixture comparison still open; headline the exact regular-region frontier and brackets, or supply that converse.

The reproduction of the quadratic-kernel variance does not yield (11): pilot-modulated inverse scores have convolutional Fourier support, including pilot frequencies, so unequal joint frequencies are not orthogonal as asserted; the proof omits the resulting cross-frequency and pilot-support terms and therefore has not established the claimed m^(4 alpha + 1) degenerate-variance bound or the advertised risk rate.

The advertised data-only honest interval is not presently evaluable: its radius depends on C_up, which is asserted computable but is supplied only existentially rather than as a stated bound or reproducible calculation from the declared class constants.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed a calibrated fixed-overlap proxy model, an equal-amplitude lower experiment, and an exact regular-region rate argument. The rough unequal-smoothness frontier remains unmatched because its correlated-sign full-likelihood converse is open; the proposed upper-risk variance proof also drops pilot-induced cross-frequency terms, and the interval constant is not yet reproducible. D0.5 rated the package subfield, below the required field floor.
tldr: For the calibrated fixed-overlap circle model, a finite deterministic two-fold deconvolved second-order estimator attains root mean-squared error \(r_n=\max\{n^{-1/2},n^{-2(s_e+s_y)/(2(s_e+s_y)+4\alpha+1)}\}\), and a class-calibrated interval has uniform \(90\%\) coverage and expected length \(O(r_n)\). The full positive-likelihood converse yields same-class equal-amplitude lower brackets indexed by \(\bar s=\max\{s_e,s_y\}\). These brackets coincide with the upper bounds throughout \(s_e+s_y\geq2\alpha+1/2\), giving an exact parametric minimax and honest-length frontier, including the boundary without logarithmic loss. Sharp nonregular unequal-smoothness lower bounds remain the explicit direct-mixture affinity question.
gap: Cui, Pu, Shi, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, Section 7 Discussion on JASA page 1357 and arXiv PDF page 28, explicitly leave low-smoothness proximal ATE minimax theory and higher-order correction open. Butucea, Theorem 2 on arXiv reprint page 14, settles the equal-smoothness quadratic benchmark, while direct-sample mixed inner products do not address the positive causal quotient or the complete two-proxy likelihood.
fill: The project derives the two-proxy information order, constructs a fully observable second-order Fourier estimator with a certified bias envelope, and seeks a same-positive-class correlation-mixture converse and matching honest interval-length lower bound that preserve the two distinct nuisance smoothness indices.
